title: Global financial crisis, deposit flight — Singapore · Indonesia (2008)
description: In October 2008 the global financial crisis reached Southeast Asian banking. On 13 October Indonesia raised its deposit insurance from Rp100 million to Rp2 billion per depositor per bank and issued emergency regulations widening Bank Indonesia's funding and creating a financial safety net. Three days later Singapore and Malaysia went further, guaranteeing all bank deposits without limit until 2010; Singapore's guarantee is backed by S$150 billion of reserves. Indonesian savers now had a reason to move money to Singapore, while Indonesia, which ended a costly blanket guarantee from the 1998 crisis only in the mid-2000s, does not want to return to one. Singapore and Indonesia must settle how Singapore's guarantee treats new deposits from Indonesia, whether Indonesia widens its own guarantee, whether Singapore offers liquidity support, and whether the two governments speak to markets together. Positions are reconstructed from the public record and are not official.

sources.title: MOF and MAS joint press statement on deposit guarantee, 16 October 2008
sources.publisher: Ministry of Finance and Monetary Authority of Singapore
facts: Singapore guaranteed all Singapore-dollar and foreign-currency deposits of individual and non-bank customers in MAS-licensed banks, finance companies and merchant banks, until 31 December 2010.
The guarantee is backed by S$150 billion of government reserves.

sources.title: Malaysia takes pre-emptive measures, 16 October 2008
facts: Malaysia's government guarantees all ringgit and foreign-currency deposits at banks regulated by Bank Negara Malaysia, through its deposit insurer PIDM, until December 2010.
Bank Negara described the measures as consistent with regional initiatives to preserve confidence in respective financial systems.

sources.title: Monetary Policy Statement, 10 October 2008
facts: MAS shifted to a zero percent appreciation of the S$NEER policy band, with no re-centring and no change to its width.
MAS cited a weakening external economy and continuing stresses in global financial markets.

sources.title: Federal Reserve and other central banks expand swap lines (press release)
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, 29 September 2008
facts: The Federal Reserve raised its US-dollar swap lines with nine central banks, all in advanced economies, to US$620 billion; no Southeast Asian central bank is among them.
